newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines enacts patent, anti-piracy law.
newsitem.headline: Philippines enacts patent, anti-piracy law.

text.p: Philippine president Fidel Ramos on Friday signed into law the country's first Intellectual Property Rights Code, one of the country's commitments to the World Trade Organisation.
The code protects local patents as well as penalises piracy of computer technology and imitation of trademarks.

"The Intellectual Property Code of 1997 will be an effective means for us to further emphasise and encourage innovation by promoting a culture of creativity, productivity and excellence," Ramos said during the signing ceremony.
Senator Raul Roco, one of the authors of the bill, said the law would stimulate the flow of technology into the country.
"With the advances in communication technology, the country now has, through the IPR Code, the necessary infrastructure to anticipate the growth and expansion ushered by these advances," Roco said.
The United States includes the Philippines on a watchlist of countries allegedly involved in widespread violation of intellectual property rights.
